topics.label: Lecture framing: initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's focus and frames how previously introduced immune components will be brought together.

topics.label: Innate danger recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain what innate recognition detects, what makes microbial patterns useful signals, and how pattern recognition receptors are encoded and positioned to detect them.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the ligands and locations of toll-like receptors and how their signaling pathways produce responses suited to the infection detected.

topics.label: Non-TLR recognition pathways and inflammasome-driven inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how other innate sensing pathways detect microbial or damage signals and can trigger inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell signaling and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells generate inflammatory signals and how those signals direct leukocytes into infected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how lymphatic drainage carries infection information and activated dendritic cells to lymph nodes to prime adaptive immune cells.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory signaling can cause systemic vasodilation, shock, and severe illness.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic distinguishes the removal of inflammatory stimuli from active signals that tell the immune response to subside.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe tissue responses when inflammation continues or fails to restore homeostasis, including repair, chronic damage, and containment of persistent infection.

topics.label: Lecture close and next-lecture notice
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and directs students to the subject of the next lecture.
